items.title: Roy Palmer Interview, 1955-09-22
items.q: Arnett Nelson used to play with us. We played at Rich Carlton.

ctx.x: Usually the trumpet player is the leader, but sometimes the trombonists and others, if you have any ideas on who should be the leader or why in New Orleans, if they usually have to come up.

I'll tell you about the bands. Like, I've seen tenor saxophones. I saw tenor saxophone lead a band. That is the leader of the band. He took the most principled parts, see, of what he had to do, of their work. He took the principled parts of it and he led the band. See, he had trumpet players there and he gave them their parts, you know, what they had to use. But he led the band off. Then it was a nice, sweet band. That's the trumpet, trumpet, tenor saxophone. Tenor saxophone, a nice instrument anyhow. Arnett…
Sure, I knew him in New York. He died too, didn't he? Yes, 1939 he died. Yeah, Tommy Latney. I heard the last records he ever made. I got to go to this session. He made it for Victor.
